content.key_idea: Capturing one CUDAGraph per strategy wastes memory linearly with strategy count; bucketing batch sizes, disaggregating target/draft capture, and merging strategies that share parameters keeps memory nearly flat while still gaining the throughput of many adaptive strategies.

summary: This figure compares three CUDAGraph-capture strategies for adaptive speculative decoding, scoring each on memory footprint and throughput. (a) Baseline: Single Strategy captures just one target+draft graph pair (V=8, D=4): Mem 1x (good) but Throughput 1x (bad), since it cannot adapt. (b) Multiple Strategies captures four full, independent strategy pairs (S1-S4, e.g. V=8/D=4 through V=48/D=8): Throughput improves to 1.8x, but Mem balloons to 4x because each strategy duplicates its own target and draft graphs. (c) Bucketed CUDAGraph Capture, the paper's own design, applies three optimizations: (i) group batch sizes into buckets B1-B4, (ii) capture target and draft graphs separately instead of paired per strategy, and (iii) merge strategies (S3, S4) that share identical parameters into one graph. The result: Mem only 1.2x while Throughput reaches 2x, winning on both axes.
summary_zh: 该图对比三种CUDAGraph捕获策略的显存与吞吐：(a)单策略显存1x但吞吐1x差；(b)四策略独立捕获吞吐1.8x但显存暴涨4x；(c)本文分桶、目标/草稿模型分离捕获并合并同参数策略，显存仅1.2x且吞吐达2x，两项均优。

The caption explicitly states the Mem/Throughput numbers are illustrative rather than measured; kept worked_example=true since the concrete values are still the content being reasoned about, but this caveat is included in provenance.evidence.
